nodes.summary: Every proposition $A$ over atoms indexed by natural numbers, built from atoms with $\land$, $\lor$ and $\to$ only, evaluates to true under the valuation that makes every atom true.
nodes.title: The all-true valuation satisfies every proposition

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram ordered from some $n$ (every tested variable is at least $n$, and tested variables strictly increase along every path). If the satisfying-path search on $t$ returns a path $p$, then $t$ evaluates to true under the assignment read off $p$.
nodes.title: The path assignment satisfies an ordered diagram

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a proposition over atoms indexed by natural numbers, let $t$ be its ROBDD, and let $f$ be a natural number. Then $A$ evaluates to true under some valuation $\sigma$ with $\sigma(f) = \mathrm{false}$ if and only if the cofactor $t[f := \mathrm{false}]$ is not the leaf $\mathrm{false}$.
nodes.title: Satisfiability with one variable fixed to false

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a binary decision diagram $t$, the existential quantification of $t$ over $x$ is the diagram obtained by combining the cofactors $t[x := \mathrm{false}]$ and $t[x := \mathrm{true}]$ with Bryant's apply under disjunction.
nodes.title: Existential quantification of a diagram

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a binary decision diagram $t$, the universal quantification of $t$ over $x$ is the diagram obtained by combining the cofactors $t[x := \mathrm{false}]$ and $t[x := \mathrm{true}]$ with Bryant's apply under conjunction.
nodes.title: Universal quantification of a diagram

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary decision diagram (tested variables strictly increase along every path), then for every variable $x$ the existential quantification of $t$ over $x$ is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram.
nodes.title: Existential quantification yields an ROBDD

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary decision diagram (tested variables strictly increase along every path), then for every variable $x$ and every Boolean $b$ the cofactor $t[x := b]$ is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram.
nodes.title: Restriction yields an ROBDD

nodes.summary: For a path $p$, given as a list of pairs $(v, b)$ of a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $b$, the assignment read off $p$ sends a variable $x$ to the Boolean of the first pair in $p$ whose variable is $x$, and to $\mathrm{false}$ if $x$ occurs in no pair of $p$.
nodes.title: Assignment read off a path

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ over atoms indexed by natural numbers, the satisfying-path search on the ROBDD of $A$ returns a path $p$, and $A$ evaluates to true under the assignment read off $p$.
nodes.title: Satisfy-one for propositions

nodes.summary: For every binary decision diagram $t$, every variable $x$ and every Boolean $b$, the cofactor $t[x := b]$ is reduced: no node has two equal children.
nodes.title: Restriction yields a reduced diagram

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a Boolean $b$, the restriction (cofactor) $t[x := b]$ of a binary decision diagram $t$ is defined recursively: a leaf is kept; a node testing $x$ is replaced by the restriction of its $\mathrm{hi}$ child if $b$ is true and of its $\mathrm{lo}$ child if $b$ is false; and a node testing any other variable $v$ is rebuilt from the restrictions of its two children with the reducing node…
nodes.title: Restriction of a binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: If a binary decision diagram $t$ is reduced and is not the leaf $\mathrm{false}$, then the search for a satisfying path in $t$ succeeds: it returns a path from the root of $t$ to a leaf $\mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Reduced diagrams other than false have a satisfying path

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a proposition over natural-number atoms and let $f$ be a natural number. If some assignment $\sigma$ with $\sigma(f) = \mathrm{false}$ satisfies $A$, then the search for a satisfying path in the restriction at $f := \mathrm{false}$ of the ROBDD of $A$ returns a path $p$, and the assignment read off $p$ (the recorded value on each variable of $p$, false elsewhere), changed to send $f$ to $\mathrm{false}$,…
nodes.title: Satisfy-one with a variable fixed to false

nodes.summary: The satisfying path of a diagram is found by a depth-first search for a leaf $\mathrm{true}$ that tries the $\mathrm{hi}$ (true) child of each node before its $\mathrm{lo}$ (false) child. It is returned as the list of pairs $(v, c)$ of the variables $v$ tested along the path with the branches $c$ taken (empty at a leaf $\mathrm{true}$), and the search returns nothing when the diagram has no leaf $\mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Satisfying path of a binary decision diagram

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
